title: Keep pi for helper work; Codex is the backup
about: pi fits small helper jobs best of 12 engines, but it has an open hang you must work around. Codex is the backup if pi breaks.

understood.label: You asked
understood.text: Which coding-agent engine should run the fleet's small helper jobs?

understood.label: Done when
understood.text: One pick and one backup, each with reasons and outside proof you can open.

understood.label: Facts as of
understood.text: 21 Oct 2026. Engines ship weekly, so check again before a switch.

visual.heading: Of 4 short-listed engines, pi fits helper jobs best
visual.text: Each tile is one short-listed engine and its verdict. The reasons are in the table below.

rows.label: pi
rows.text: Small, any model, scripted mode. One open hang.

rows.label: Codex CLI
rows.text: Strong scripted mode. Other models are rough.

rows.label: OpenCode
rows.text: Major upgrade now, and a key leak on 17 Oct.

rows.label: Goose
rows.text: Scripted mode misses hooks; smaller field use.

details.label: Engines surveyed
details.value: 12, from 9 comparison posts, GitHub and Hacker News

sections.heading: I looked at 12 engines and cut 8
sections.body: A helper job needs any model, a scripted mode with no screen, and an open licence. Each cut misses one of these.

items.title: Claude Code: cut
items.text: Anthropic models only, and not open source.
items.more: Checked: the GitHub repository states no licence (github.com/anthropics/claude-code). It stays the right engine for main workers, not for cheap helpers.

items.title: Gemini CLI: cut
items.more: Reported: comparison posts rank it high for scripted output (kilo.ai/articles/best-cli-coding-agents), but other models are not its main path.

items.title: Qwen Code: cut
items.text: A Gemini CLI fork tuned for Qwen models.
items.more: Reported: it follows Gemini CLI and adds the Qwen route (github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code).

items.title: Aider: cut
items.more: Checked: the last release is v0.86.0 on 9 Aug 2025 and the last push was 22 May 2026 (github.com/Aider-AI/aider/releases).

items.title: Crush: cut
items.text: Its licence is not marked open source.
items.more: Checked: GitHub shows no recognised licence for github.com/charmbracelet/crush. I did not read the licence text in full.

items.title: Amp, Cursor CLI, Droid: cut
items.more: Reported: each is a paid hosted product (ai.dosa.dev/best/ai-coding-agents-for-terminal). I did not test them.

items.title: Cline CLI and Kilo: cut
items.text: Editor-first tools with a newer command line.
items.more: Reported: both grew from editor add-ons (kilo.ai/articles/best-cli-coding-agents). I did not test them.

sections.heading: The 4 short-listed engines on the same 5 points
sections.body: Each row gives: models, scripted mode, known breaks, how the makers answer, and safety. Tap a row for all 5.

items.title: pi: the pick
items.text: Pros: any model, small, scripted mode. Cons: one open hang.
items.more: Models: any, through providers. Scripted: yes, with JSON output (bitdoze.com/opencode-vs-pi-agent). Breaks: hangs when its input pipe stays open (github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10415); can switch model silently (issues/10623). Makers: auto-close new issues, then reopen real ones; both are reopened. Safety: no leak reported.

items.title: Codex CLI: the backup
items.text: Pros: mature scripted mode. Cons: other models are rough, adds a daemon.
items.more: Models: OpenAI first; others through its provider settings, with open gaps (github.com/openai/codex/issues/26234). Scripted: yes, with JSON output. Breaks: exec can hang on a stalled stream (issues/50775); a maker replied the same day. Safety: installs a self-updating background service (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50060694).

items.title: OpenCode: not now
items.text: Pros: many features, any model. Cons: forced major upgrade, key leak.
items.more: Models: any. Scripted: yes. Breaks: version 1 now gets only critical fixes (github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57661); stream errors retry forever with no message (issues/49030). Makers: a bot answers first. Safety: keys saved in its web workspace may have leaked on 17 Oct (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50133401).

items.title: Goose: not now
items.text: Pros: open, active. Cons: scripted mode misses hooks.
items.more: Models: any. Scripted: yes. Breaks: hooks do not run in scripted mode with some providers (github.com/aaif-goose/goose/issues/12746); a system prompt is ignored when an instructions file is given (issues/12682). Makers: a maintainer explained the cause. Safety: no leak reported. Field use: no large discussion found on Hacker News this year.

sections.heading: What I checked myself
sections.body: These I ran or read at the source on 21 Oct 2026.

items.title: pi hangs on an open input pipe
items.text: pi 1.0.0 in scripted mode did not finish while its input stayed open.
items.more: I ran pi in scripted mode with its input left open for 12 seconds and a 6-second limit. It was stopped by the limit, as issue 10415 says. Starting pi with its input closed is the work-around.

items.title: Release dates and licences
items.text: Read from GitHub for all 9 open repositories.
items.more: Last releases: pi 15 Oct, Codex 15 Oct, OpenCode 16 Oct, Goose 16 Oct 2026; Aider 9 Aug 2025. Licences: MIT for pi and OpenCode, Apache 2.0 for Codex and Goose.

sections.heading: What others report, and what I could not read
sections.body: These are claims by others. I opened each link but did not repeat their tests.

items.title: pi is lean and saves tokens
items.text: Its author and a 100-hour test say so.
items.more: news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46844822 (173 comments) and composio.dev/blog/pi-vs-opencode. Both favour pi on speed and control and OpenCode on features.

items.title: OpenCode 2.0 is a big change
items.text: Users like it, but it changes tool names.
items.more: news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50094994 and the upgrade note in github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57661.

items.title: Could not read Reddit or X
items.text: Reddit refused the fetch; X needs a browser login.
items.more: Reddit answered 403 to search. The OpenCode post on X (x.com/opencode) did not load without JavaScript; I used the team's copy on Hacker News instead.

sections.heading: Keep pi, and fix how we start it
sections.body: pi is the pick. Codex CLI is the runner-up if pi's hang is not fixed soon.

items.title: Pick: pi
items.text: Any model, the smallest engine, and its makers reopened both bugs.
items.more: The hang has a simple work-around: always start pi with its input closed. Pin the version and read the change notes before each update.

items.title: Runner-up: Codex CLI
items.text: The most mature scripted mode, with fast maker replies.
items.more: It loses first place because other models are a side path with open gaps, and it adds a background service we would have to turn off.

items.title: Look again on 21 Nov 2026
items.text: OpenCode 2 may settle, and pi may fix issue 10415.
items.more: Re-check the 4 short-listed engines then, with the same 5 points.
